About 10–30 preceding turns seem to be enough for most of the gain in identifying a speaker’s emotion or mood: one ERC study found conversational context is the main driver, but performance saturates quickly, with roughly 90% of the benefit captured within the most recent 10–30 prior turns, and strong results are achievable using only past turns in a strictly causal setup [1]. A related paper also argues that speaker mood often persists across multiple utterances and can be better recognized by modeling each speaker’s emotional history and likely emotion shifts [6].

On sentence starters, the supplied papers do not study generic sentence-openers directly, but one paper does analyze discourse-marker position and finds emotion is reliably associated with where markers appear: sad utterances use fewer left-periphery markers than other emotions, suggesting weaker local pragmatic cues and greater dependence on context [1]. A different paper on “starters” is about personalized conversation-opening prompts for initiating chats, not identifying mood within an ongoing conversation [10].
